sections.title: Consumer Apps
sections.subtitle: A curated portfolio of consumer applications I've had the opportunity to work on across the B2C healthcare and technology industries. Click on any tile to learn more about each project.

cards.title: Scheduling: Set Your Working Hours
cards.problem: Our marketplace is supply-constrained because we ask therapists to elect their hours, and we're only showing 25% of the time slots our competitors are showing.
cards.metrics:
Primary: Doubled the amount of therapist availability per week
Secondary: $2M in ARR
cards.solutionSummary: Therapists set working hours, and we generate bookable time slots for clients. Anything outside of busy times from Google Calendar within working hours is considered a time slot.
cards.solution:
Therapists set working hours, and we generate bookable time slots for clients. Anything outside of busy times from Google Calendar within working hours is considered a time slot.

The calendar app is now a bi-directional sync between a therapist's Google Calendar and our system. The system uses Cobalt RPA to mock the add availability API endpoint, and the Nylas Calendar API to facilitate read and write scopes for bi-directional Google Calendar authentication.

This solution reduced schedule management effort by 75%, increasing therapist availability by 1.5× to support 200 additional quarterly bookings and $2M ARR, while mitigating scheduling conflicts for 9K clients without follow-up appointments.

Click the Add working hours button to see this functionality live!

cards.title: Scheduling: Enter Your Availability in 3 Clicks
cards.problem: High-friction availability creation (12 clicks per timeslot in the EHR) artifically constraints supply and causes therapist frustration.
cards.metrics:
Primary: Added 2 hours of therapist availability per week
Secondary: $1M in ARR
cards.solutionSummary: Therapists can update their availability in just 3 clicks, directly from the new calendar app in the Therapist Portal.
cards.solution:
Therapists can update their availability in just 3 clicks, directly from the new calendar app in the Therapist Portal. The calendar shows both Google and EHR appointments in one place, decreasing the time to add new availabilty by 75%.

The scheduling system was built using Cobalt RPA to mock the add availability API endpoint, and the Nylas Calendar API to facilitate read-only scopes for Google Calendar authentication.

Click the Add availability button to see this functionality live!

cards.title: Daily Dashboard for Therapists
cards.problem: Workflows spread across 4+ disparate systems; current daily email has stale data and <10% click rate despite >85% open rate.
cards.solutionSummary: Therapists can start their day with real-time insights served over a dashboard with caseload insights, one-click access to telehealth appointments, and actionable metrics.
cards.solution: Therapists can start their day with real-time insights served over a dashboard with caseload insights, one-click access to telehealth appointments, and actionable metrics. The team created new REST endpoints to aggregate caseload data from our therapist and client tables, in addition to linking measures information from Blueprint.

cards.title: QA: Bulk Clinical Note Review
cards.problem: It takes 6 months for therapists to receive feedback from our QA team, because each therapist's case requires 2 hours of manual review.
cards.solutionSummary: Our QA team can now review clinical notes, detect duplicate notes, and automatically email therapists with feedback from the same place.
cards.solution: Our QA team can now review clinical notes, detect duplicate notes, and automatically email therapists with feedback from the same place. We built this app using Retool, which generates a skeleton UI to pull note data from our EHR notes database and allows us to call the MailMerge API to send feedback to therapists over email.

cards.title: Manage Your Caseload
cards.problem: Therapists navigate 10+ disconnected systems to find basic client info; no accurate centralized caseload view in Therapist Portal.
cards.solutionSummary: Therapists can see a list of their active and past clients, including recommended next steps and when their last appointment with their client was.
cards.solution:
Therapists can see a list of their active and past clients, including recommended next steps and when their last appointment with their client was. To pull all relevant information to generate the client list, we updated existing GraphQL endpoints to query the client's name, insurance, and next appointment information from our therapist, client, and appointment tables.

We counted how many appointments they have to calculate whether they need measures, and we derived the value of status based on whether the client was net-new, had already seen their therapist, or needed to be closed out due to inactivity.

cards.title: Multi-State Practice
cards.problem: Therapists licensed in multiple states can only practice in one, limiting supply in new markets and national payer attractiveness.
cards.metrics: Increase supply within our existing network by 10%
cards.solutionSummary: Therapists can update their availability to see clients in multiple states.
cards.solution: Therapists can update their availability to see clients in multiple states. Our Therapist Portal and EHR now supports updating schedules and billing claims for multiple states. This expands the number of covered lives per therapist. This involved schema changes in our billing databases and forward compatibility with OpenPM integrations.

cards.title: In-Person Appointments
cards.problem: 40%+ of therapy clients prefer in-person care, but we don't offer any in-person appointments.
cards.metrics: Increase supply within our existing network by 15%
cards.solutionSummary: Therapists can update their schedule to specify when they are available for in-person appointments.
cards.solution: Therapists can update their schedule to specify when they are available for in-person appointments. Our EHR and therapist-facing tooling now supports in-person appointment options. We updated our billing system to differentiate between in-person and telehealth appointment claims. This involved schema changes in our billing databases and forward compatibility with OpenPM integrations.

cards.title: Zingo: An App for Solo Travelers
cards.problem: Solo travelers have a hard time finding activities and events to do in a new city.
cards.solutionSummary: We built Zingo, a social network for solo travelers to find events and activities to do in a new city.
cards.solution: We built Zingo, a social network for solo travelers to find events and activities to do in a new city. The app was created using Vue and Firebase, and uses the Google Maps API to display events and activities in a new city.

cards.title: Lend a Hand: Social Media Content Moderation
cards.problem: For some users struggling with their mental health, sharing on social media can be cathartic. For others, seeing these details can be triggering and even detrimental. Those who are actively at risk of self-harm or suicidal ideation need immediate support.
cards.solutionSummary: Lend a Hand is a Chrome extension that serves as a preventative safety net to redirect users who are at risk of self-harm or suicidal ideation to live-time resources and support.
cards.solution: Lend a Hand is a Chrome extension that serves as a preventative safety net to redirect users who are at risk of self-harm or suicidal ideation to live-time resources and support. It was built using Flask and the Microsoft Cognitive Services API to process language and evaluate it for content moderation risk.

sections.title: Business Integrations
sections.subtitle: A curated portfolio of business integrations I've had the opportunity to work on across the B2C healthcare and technology industries. Click on any tile to learn more about each project.

cards.title: Google Calendar Integration
cards.problem: Therapists double-book with competitors because our appointments aren't visible on their Google Calendar.
cards.metrics:
Primary: Doubled the amount of therapist availability per week
Secondary: $2M in ARR
cards.solutionSummary: Therapists now have access to an outbound Google Calendar sync to write appointments back to the therapist's Google Calendar.
cards.solution:
Therapists now have access to an outbound Google Calendar sync to write appointments back to the therapist's Google Calendar. This allows therapists to see their entire work schedule from Google Calendar, decreasing the chance that they will be double-booked with competitors.

The app supports up to 9 calendars and 3 Google accountsm using read and write scopes requested from Google and Nylas Calendar API to support bi-directional authentication.

cards.title: Zendesk Support Chatbot
cards.problem: After a major workflow change, we saw a 5× increase in therapist-submitted support tickets. With only Slack to triage requests, our operational teams were severely bottlenecked.
cards.metrics:
Primary: Therapist NPS
Secondary: Decrease support tickets by 20%
cards.solutionSummary: Therapists can now use a Zendesk live chat widget in the Therapist Portal to self-serve questions and receive immediate support.
cards.solution: Therapists can now use a Zendesk live chat widget in the Therapist Portal to self-serve questions and receive immediate support. The widget was set up as a self-improving AI agent using Zendesk AI agents. This decreased support ticket volume by 20%, improved Portal utilization, and boosted overall therapist satisfaction.

cards.title: Streamlined Zendesk Support Queues
cards.problem: Therapists request support via Gmail and Slack, creating untrackable, unsecured requests with long turnaround times.
cards.solutionSummary: Therapists can message staff via the Therapist Portal, which creates a Zendesk message. This scales to our support volume of 2000+ tickets/month and allows staff to triage replies.
cards.solution:
Therapists can message staff via the Therapist Portal, which creates a Zendesk message. This scales to our support volume of 2000+ tickets/month and allows staff to triage replies. The app was created using Zendesk Messaging SDK.

We created custom React components for each message, allowing therapists to send outbound messages directly from the Portal and for staff to reply directly from Zendesk.

cards.title: Therapist Database: A Single Source of Truth
cards.problem: Therapist data lacks a single source of truth, fragmented across Airtable, Zoho, and Zapier with no defined schema — causing recurring sync failures, operational brittleness, and reliance on manual file uploads.
cards.metrics: Primary: Number of systems required to process a new therapist record
cards.solutionSummary: We built a new relational SQL database as the internal source of truth for therapist data, standardizing the data coming from the upstream Airtable integration.
cards.solution:
We built a new relational SQL database as the internal source of truth for therapist data, standardizing the data coming from the upstream Airtable integration.

This new database is a single point of truth for therapist data across all therapist directories and internal booking pages, replacing the fragmented Airtable, Zoho, and Zapier integrations. It checks for new data daily, updates 50+ data fields to generate 15k provider bios weekly, and serves consumer requests at 99.9% availability.

Under my leadership, we published V1 and V2 endpoints for other services (scheduling, client booking, external insurance directories) to access.

cards.title: Onboard Partner Therapist Network
cards.problem: We needed to onboard 10K+ therapists from a new partnership network, but our current onboarding process didn't scale to this volume.
cards.solutionSummary: We reused our existing Tellescope CRM instance to build no-code workflows for therapists to complete enrollment, automate operational workflows (background checks, credentialing, etc.), and receive branded communications.
cards.solution:
My team built an end-to-end provider onboarding experience for our B2B2C partnership with a major insurance provider.

We reused our existing Tellescope CRM instance to build no-code workflows for therapists to complete enrollment, automate operational workflows (background checks, credentialing, etc.), and receive branded communications.

The Tellescope journeys were integrated with Tray.ai agentic workflows, supporting 10K eligible providers while reducing manual operational work by 50%.

cards.title: Faster New Hire Onboarding
cards.problem: Therapist onboarding requires therapists to navigate 6+ systems, lacks the visibility for staff to trace progress end-to-end, and takes 47 days on average. The process is cumbersome enough to cause significant attrition.
cards.solutionSummary: In partnership with Clinical Ops and Credentialing, we reduced provider onboarding time by 25% and saved $600K annually by auditing 10+ software systems, deprecating 3 of them, and replacing them with Tellescope CRM and Zendesk AI chatbot.
cards.solution:
In partnership with Clinical Ops and Credentialing, we reduced provider onboarding time by 25% and saved $600K annually by auditing 10+ software systems and deprecating 3 of them.

We implemented a bidirectional sync between our Therapist Database and Tellescope CRM, where Tellescope is used as an environment to store therapist lead data. This enables us to retire Airtable upstream and integrate Tellescope as the only CRM for therapist information.

cards.title: Faster Invoice Processing
cards.problem: Since we run a bimonthly payroll, therapists get paid on different days of the week. Our contracted therapists rely on consistent pay dates.
cards.solutionSummary: All therapists are now paid biweekly on the same dates each month. This updated schedule improves therapist satisfaction and reduced the time to pay by 25%.
cards.solution: This initiative required cross-functional buy-in with Finance, Product Ops, and our external insurance partners so we could productionize a biweekly pay schedule to pay contracted providers on fixed days of the month. All therapists are now paid biweekly on the same dates each month. This updated schedule improves therapist satisfaction and reduced the time to pay by 25%.

cards.title: Streamline Payment Infrastructure For Faster Payouts
cards.problem: Each appointment required 6+ hours to sync between our systems before it could be processed for payment, requiring 15+ hrs of manual intervention per pay period.
cards.metrics:
Primary: Time to sync (6 hrs → 20 minutes)
Secondary: Reduce ZD tickets by 50%
cards.solutionSummary: We reduced the time to sync updates to appointments by 95% by creating a new microservice that syncs appointment data to the payment processing system.
cards.solution: We reduced the time to sync updates to appointments by 95% by creating a new microservice that syncs appointment data to the payment processing system. Previously, the average case to sync a single update would take 1.5 hrs, and the new infrastructure reduced average time to under 2 minutes. This change improved therapist NPS and reduced Zendesk support tickets by 15%.

cards.title: CRM for White-Glove Client Leads
cards.problem: To match a single client to a therapist, our white-glove care navigation team used 5+ spreadsheets to track client info and preferences. This process was tedious, taking 2 hours to match a client to a therapist. Our teams also couldn't track a client's progress through care after the initial match.
cards.solutionSummary: Tellescope CRM now replaces the matching spreadsheets with an agentic ticketing workflow, reducing the time to match a client to a therapist by 75%.
cards.solution: I stood up a new instance of Tellescope CRM to replace the matching spreadsheets with an agentic ticketing workflow. Much of our white glove matching teams' workflows still exist in this CRM instance today, allowing the matching team to track a client's lifecycle end-to-end. This initiative reduced the time to match a client to a therapist by 75%.
